findings.reading: 458 of 500 rows sit at KD 10 or below, so the SERPs are open. They are simply not about journeys between two named places. This matches the phrasing correction already banked, where "von berlin nach" resolved to the parent topic "flug berlin paris": German demand for a city pair is expressed as a flight search, which is a booking intent Livdar cannot serve and should not try to.
findings.consequence_for_the_plan: the transport pair axis must NOT be fanned out across the fifteen languages on the assumption that English demand implies demand elsewhere. English carries it (346 of 500 rows name two places). German does not (2 of 500). Each further language needs its own probe before any pages are built for it, and the projected language-scoped transport yield of roughly 74,000 pages has to be treated as unproven rather than pending.
